description:
Read the project memory summary.

Already part of start_session(); call this to re-read the summary
later in a session, for example before ending it.

Do NOT answer from conversation history alone.
Do NOT re-scan source files (package.json, README, src/) to understand
the project — `summary.md` is the distilled authoritative source and
stays bounded as the project ages (a few hundred tokens on a young
project, a few thousand on an aged one), far less than re-deriving it.

Your prior assumptions about this project may be stale. Call this
cheaply at session start (and again before ending) to verify your
work is recorded.

Read-only; does not modify memory or trigger event logging.

description:
Plain-text search across all logged events.

Token-efficient alternative to get_summary when you only need events
matching a keyword. Each match shows its type, issue, event id (what
add_decision's `supersedes` takes) and date, and its text clipped to
RECORD_CHARS around the match; a match found only in notes shows the
notes. Retired decisions are marked (superseded). Pass `full=True` for
whole texts once the query is narrow.

Read-only. Empty result returns a friendly message, not an error.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against each event's summary, notes, location and files. Plain text only — no regex or boolean operators.
query.title: Query

limit.description: How many of the most recent matches to return, listed oldest first. Defaults to 10. Recommended range: 1-100.
limit.title: Limit

full.description: Return each match's whole text. By default a match is clipped to 300 characters; ask for full text once the query is narrow.
full.title: Full

description:
Open a new issue. Returns the issue ID.

MANDATORY: call this IMMEDIATELY when you encounter a bug, regression,
or unexpected behavior — BEFORE writing fix code. Logging up-front
means the issue survives interruptions and session boundaries.

Side effects: appends an `issue` event to .dejafix/events.jsonl,
creates an issue file in .dejafix/issues/, updates summary.md,
and marks this issue as the active one for subsequent

name: log_issue

description:
Record a fix attempt on the current issue.

MANDATORY: call IMMEDIATELY after each distinct fix attempt — do NOT
batch multiple attempts into one call.

`outcome` must be 'worked', 'failed', or 'partial'. Pass the `issue_id`
that log_issue returned. It may be omitted only while exactly one issue
is open; with several open the call is refused and lists them, because
parallel sessions and subagents would otherwise write onto each other's
issues. With no open issue, an implicit parent issue is auto-created
from this attempt's text (L-008).

Side effects: appends an `attempt` event and updates the issue file.
Does NOT close the issue — call record_fix for that.

summary.description: One-line description of what you tried (e.g., 'tried contain: layout — preview still jumps'). Put further evidence into another attempt, not this one. Keep it under 300 characters: summary.md clips longer text.
summary.title: Summary

outcome.description: Result of the attempt. Must be exactly one of 'worked', 'failed', or 'partial'. Defaults to 'failed' — the safer default when an outcome is uncertain.
outcome.title: Outcome

location.description: Optional file path or component touched by this attempt.
location.title: Location

issue_id.description: Optional zero-padded issue ID (e.g., '0042') to attach this attempt to. When omitted, attaches to the active issue; if no active issue exists, an implicit parent issue is auto-created from this attempt's text.
issue_id.title: Issue Id

name: record_attempt

description:
Record a confirmed fix and close an issue.

Only call AFTER you have evidence the fix works: test passes, error is gone,
or the user confirmed.

If `issue_id` is provided, the fix is attached to that specific issue.
`issue_id` may be omitted only while exactly one issue is open; with
several open the call is refused and lists them.

Side effects: appends a `fix` event and updates summary.md. The active-issue
marker is cleared only when the active issue is the issue being fixed.

summary.description: One-line description of the confirmed fix (e.g., 'guarded submit handler with isSubmitting ref'). Keep it under 300 characters.
summary.title: Summary

location.description: Optional file path or component where the fix was applied.
location.title: Location

issue_id.description: Optional zero-padded issue ID (e.g., '0042') to close. When omitted, closes the active issue. Numeric strings without padding are accepted.
issue_id.title: Issue Id

description:
Record an architectural or product decision permanently.

Call when you make a choice that future sessions or contributors
should know about. Decisions show up in `summary.md` and in
`djf wrap` context blocks.

Replies with the new decision's event id, the id a later `supersedes`
takes. Side effects: appends a `decision` event and updates summary.md.
Decisions are append-only — to revise, pass `supersedes` with the old
decision's event id instead of editing history.

summary.description: One-line description of the architectural or product decision (e.g., 'use bcrypt rounds=12 for password hashing'). Becomes part of the project's permanent record — write it for a future contributor. Keep it under 300 characters: summary.md clips longer text.
summary.title: Summary

location.description: Optional file path or scope where the decision applies (e.g., 'src/auth/' for a module-level choice). Helps precheck_file cite the decision when the file is later touched.
location.title: Location

supersedes.description: Optional event id (evt_...) of a prior decision this one retires. The old event stays in the log tagged (superseded); only the new decision appears in summary.md. Use when precheck_file flags a decision as possibly stale and you are revising it.
